note: The cases of the Drawing Format Standard conformance suite. See clause 17.

cases.description: Lines: model to paper, widths from layer roles, role and line type override, a duplicate kept, unsorted input.
A closed and an open polyline.
Arcs with sweeps 90, 180 and 270 (worked numbers of clause 9.5.2).
Circles: the radius is scaled, the line type comes from the layer.
A centre line is a line: default thin and chain, and an override.
Hatches: a solid hatch with a hole (no marks) and a lines hatch (marks are entities).
Pattern lines at angle 0: horizontal lines every 1.8 mm, split by a hole (clause 10.5.9).
Pattern lines at angle 45: the frame is turned; line ends are not exact in binary.
Pattern soil: lines of line type dashed.
Pattern water: lines every 3.6 mm (clause 10.5.9).
Pattern concrete: dots on even rows, triangles on odd rows, none within the clearance of an edge.
Pattern rockfill: pentagons on a staggered lattice.
Pattern concrete at angle 30: marks turn with the frame.
Pattern lines in a viewport turned by 90: the hatch angle becomes 90, so the lines are vertical.
Pattern solid draws no marks.
On A0 the hatch unit is 3.5 mm.
Text: height, alignment and paper rotation are copied; the anchor is mapped.
Rotation 90: points turn, arc start and hatch angle add 90, text rotation is unchanged.
Rotation 40.25: values that are not exact in binary, away from rounding ties.
Line group 0.7 on A0: OUTLINE 0.7, HIDDEN 0.35 dashed, PIPE 1.4.
Line group 0.35 on A3: OUTLINE 0.35, HIDDEN 0.18 dashed, PIPE 0.7 (clause 8.7.1).
A custom layer gives its role and line type.
Right-aligned text whose anchor is 5 mm from the frame edge: the box ends at the anchor and fits.
A horizontal linear dimension of an 8 m line, 10 mm below it (worked by hand in the standard).
A vertical linear dimension: the text turns to read upwards.
The unit mm gives the text 8000 with 0 decimals.
Three decimals and text height 2.5.
Point specs with literal points; a positive offset puts the line on the left of D.
An aligned dimension of the 3-4-5 triangle: value 5.00, direction (0.6, -0.8).
Radius of a circle in the default direction 45 degrees: R1.50.
Diameter of a circle with the line vertical: the text reads upwards.
Radius of an arc, with a direction inside the sweep.
A right angle: 90.0 degrees with a dimension arc of 15 mm.
An angle between two lines by reference: atan2(4, 2) = 63.43 degrees.
A leader to the right: the label is left-aligned.
A leader to the left: the label is right-aligned.
A horizontal dimension in a viewport turned by 90 degrees: the model x axis goes up the sheet.
A chain: parts 2.50, 2.50, 2.50 and overall 7.50.
Parts print 1.25 three times (3.75) but the overall prints 3.76 (clause 12.8.1).
A chain with no overall.
A reference to an id that does not exist.
A line has no centre place.
A radius dimension must point at a circle or an arc.
Two points with the same x give the horizontal value 0.
3 mm between the arrowheads is less than 2a = 7.2 mm.
A dimension line 0.5 mm from the point leaves no extension line (gap u/2 = 0.9 mm).
The dimension line is 120 mm below the points, below the frame.
The direction 180 is outside the sweep 0 to 90 of the arc.
R is 5 mm, less than 2a = 7.2 mm.
A ray of length 0.
The leader and its label are at one point.
A paper_mm symbol with a label: 0.1 m per mm of symbol at 1:100 (worked in clause 13.4.1).
The same symbol at 1:200: the same size on the paper.
Insert scale 2 doubles a paper_mm symbol on the paper.
A model_m symbol is a real size: 2 m wide, 20 mm on the paper at 1:100. Circle, arc, solid hatch and a default label slot.
The same model_m symbol at 1:200: half the size on the paper.
Rotation 90 about the insertion point; the label stays upright on the paper.
Rotation 30: values that are not exact in binary.
A viewport turned by 90: the symbols turn with the model; arc angles add 90.
A part takes the role and line type of the layer, or the role of the insert, unless it has its own.
The library is a file next to the document.
Dimensions and leaders point at ports: the gap between two valves is 4.00 - 0.6 m.
The library has no symbol of that name.
The document has no library of that id.
The library file cannot be read.
The library file has a member that the schema does not know.
A line of length 0 in a symbol.
Two libraries with one id.
A library with both path and symbols (schema error).
Insert scale 0 (schema error).
A label on a symbol with no label slot.
The symbol lands beyond the right edge of the frame.
The symbol has no port of that name.
The ISO 7200 template with the three required fields; scale and size are derived.
Every given field, and the derived sheet number 2/5.
Two sealed revisions: the approver, checker and revision come only from the latest entry (clause 14.4.2).
Eight entries fill the register: no overflow row.
Eleven entries: the overflow row stands first and says 4 EARLIER REVISIONS NOT SHOWN.
Nine entries: the overflow row says 2 EARLIER REVISIONS NOT SHOWN.
The numeric scheme: 1, 2, 10 rise. Equal dates are allowed.
An entry without a seal is allowed (only a seal that does not match is an error).
Alpha tokens rise Z, AA.
The DRAFT status line: height 2.5 at the bottom-left of the drawing space, with its reserved region.
The CONCEPT status line.
Issued: the latest entry has an approver and a valid seal; no status line.
The DRAFT line stands on the last line of the notes strip; no title block.
The CONCEPT line stands on the last line of the notes strip, above the title block.
Issued shows no status line; the strip keeps the whole of its height for the notes.
The CONCEPT line at the bottom-left; the title block stands at the bottom-right.
A notes strip too low for its heading and the status line.
A frame over the region of the status line.
Two viewports with different scales: the scale cell says AS SHOWN.
On A4 portrait the drawing space is 180 mm wide, the same as the block.
On A0 (line group 0.7) the lines of the block are 0.7 and 0.35 mm wide.
A template passed by path: 100 x 30 mm, a register of 3 rows (so 5 entries show an overflow row), and right and centre alignment.
A notes strip on the right and a references strip at the bottom of the strip area (above the title block).
With no title block the strip area is the whole drawing space.
A template id that the standard does not ship.
The template file cannot be read.
The template file has a member that the schema does not know.
Two cells overlap.
The required field owner is missing.
The private template has no cell for document_type.
The title is 5 mm high and does not fit 108 mm: it is an error, never cut.
The description is wider than its 98 mm cell.
Two entries with the rev A.
The tokens A, B, B do not rise.
The second date is before the first.
30 February does not exist.
A sealed entry was edited. The edited entry and the one after it no longer match their seals.
An entry inserted between sealed entries: the seal of the one after it fails.
Issued, but the latest entry has no approver. An approver on an earlier entry does not count.
Issued, but the latest entry has no seal.
Issued, but there is no revision register.
Issued, but there is no title block.
The strip is wider than the strip area.
Two strips for the notes.
Notes, and no strip to put them in.
A note wider than the strip.
Sixty notes do not fit the height of the strip.
A block 200 mm wide in a drawing space 180 mm wide.
The frame of the viewport covers the corner of the title block.
A template and a template path (schema error).
The status final does not exist (schema error).
A seal that is not sha256:<64 hex> (schema error).

Start 45 and end 405 give a sweep of 0.

xmax equals xmin.
